name: Reinforcement Learning
description: Learning by trial and error: MDPs, tabular methods, deep Q-learning, policy gradients and modern RL.

nodes.name: The RL problem
nodes.desc: Agents, environments, states, actions, rewards and returns.
nodes.summary: You will be able to frame a decision problem as an agent interacting with an environment to maximise cumulative reward.

nodes.name: Multi-armed bandits
nodes.desc: Exploration versus exploitation with epsilon-greedy, UCB and Thompson sampling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to balance exploration and exploitation in multi-armed bandits with epsilon-greedy, UCB and Thompson sampling.

nodes.name: MDPs
nodes.desc: Markov decision processes, policies, discounting and value functions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to formalise sequential decision problems as Markov decision processes with policies and value functions.
topics: MDP tuple of states, actions, transitions and rewards

nodes.name: Bellman equations
nodes.desc: Bellman expectation and optimality equations for state and action values.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write and interpret Bellman expectation and optimality equations for state and action values.

nodes.name: Value iteration
nodes.desc: Policy evaluation, policy iteration and value iteration when the model is known.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute optimal policies with dynamic programming when the environment model is known.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo methods
nodes.desc: Learning values from complete episodes without a model.
nodes.summary: You will be able to estimate values and improve policies from complete episodes without a model of the environment.

nodes.name: TD learning
nodes.desc: Temporal-difference updates, TD(0) and SARSA.
nodes.summary: You will be able to learn values from incomplete episodes with temporal-difference updates and control with SARSA.

nodes.name: Q-learning
nodes.desc: Off-policy control with Q-learning and its convergence intuition.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement off-policy Q-learning and explain why it converges toward optimal action values.

nodes.name: Gridworld agent
nodes.desc: Implement and compare value iteration, SARSA and Q-learning on gridworlds.
nodes.summary: You will implement value iteration, SARSA and Q-learning on gridworlds and compare their learned policies and learning speed.

nodes.name: Function approximation
nodes.desc: Linear and neural value functions and the deadly triad.
nodes.summary: You will be able to approximate value functions with linear and neural models and explain the instability of the deadly triad.
topics: Why tabular methods do not scale

nodes.name: Deep Q-networks
nodes.desc: DQN with experience replay and target networks, and later improvements.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how DQN stabilises deep Q-learning with experience replay and target networks and how later variants improve it.

nodes.name: Exploration
nodes.desc: Exploration strategies for large state spaces, including count-based and curiosity methods.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose exploration strategies for large state spaces, including count-based bonuses and curiosity-driven methods.
topics: Optimism in the face of uncertainty

nodes.name: Policy gradients
nodes.desc: The policy gradient theorem, REINFORCE and baselines.
nodes.summary: You will be able to derive the policy gradient theorem and train policies directly with REINFORCE and baselines.

nodes.name: Actor-critic
nodes.desc: Combining a learned policy and value function, A2C and advantage estimation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to combine a learned policy with a learned value function in actor-critic methods such as A2C.

nodes.name: PPO
nodes.desc: Trust regions and clipped objectives for stable policy optimisation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how trust regions and PPO's clipped objective make policy optimisation stable.

nodes.name: Control agent
nodes.desc: Train agents on classic control and Atari-style tasks and analyse learning curves.
nodes.summary: You will train agents on classic control and Atari-style tasks and analyse their learning curves and failure modes.
topics: Training a DQN or PPO agent

nodes.name: Model-based RL
nodes.desc: Learning environment models, planning and Monte Carlo tree search.
nodes.summary: You will be able to learn environment models and use them for planning, including Monte Carlo tree search.

nodes.name: Offline RL
nodes.desc: Learning policies from fixed datasets and the distribution shift problem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to learn policies from fixed datasets and explain how distribution shift makes offline RL difficult.

nodes.name: Multi-agent RL
nodes.desc: Cooperative and competitive settings, self-play and non-stationarity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse cooperative and competitive multi-agent settings and explain self-play and non-stationarity.

nodes.name: RL from human feedback
nodes.desc: Reward models from human preferences and RL fine-tuning of language models.
nodes.summary: You will understand how reward models are trained from human preferences and used to fine-tune language models with RL.
topics: KL penalty to a reference model
